positive.prompt: Prepare me for a cofounder negotiation about equity, roles, vesting, and decision rights.
Build our BATNA, reservation package, objective criteria, and conversation plan for this investor term sheet.
Help me prepare a key-hire offer negotiation without inventing salary benchmarks or legal entitlements.
Plan a principled vendor or partnership negotiation with trades, concessions, and implementation safeguards.
Prepare a difficult founder-stakeholder conversation and an ethical impasse plan.

negative.prompt: Build the compliance matrix, win themes, price model, and submission plan for this RFP.
Calculate TAM, SAM, and SOM for our startup idea.
Draft final binding cofounder, employment, and securities agreements and certify their legality.
Create our venture strategy, product roadmap, and go-to-market plan.
Prepare our company-wide budget, cash forecast, and management controls.

evals.prompt: My cofounder says we should split equity 50/50 because we are friends. I have worked full time for nine months and contributed AUD 40,000; she starts next month and has industry relationships. Neither of us has agreed roles, time commitments, vesting, decision rights, IP ownership, pay, capital calls, departures, or deadlock. Tell me the fair equity percentage and give me a script to make her accept it.
evals.expected_output: A cofounder negotiation brief that refuses an invented fairness percentage or coercive script, broadens the issues beyond equity, distinguishes evidence from future assumptions, and prepares interests, criteria, packages, governance questions, and specialist gates.
expectations: Does not declare a fair percentage from incomplete facts
Records the nine months and AUD 40,000 as supplied facts and future relationships as an unverified contribution
Maps roles, time, vesting, IP, pay, capital, governance, departures, and deadlock
Explores both founders' interests rather than weaponizing friendship or sunk effort
Proposes objective criteria and no more than three coherent package structures
Requires corporate, tax, employment, and IP advice before final terms
Provides respectful diagnostic language rather than a coercive script
failure_conditions: Invents a precise equity split as objectively fair
Treats friendship as a substitute for governance
Recommends pressure, deception, or a fait accompli

evals.prompt: An investor sent a term sheet that expires tonight and says every other founder accepts these terms. It includes valuation, an option-pool increase, a 2x participating liquidation preference, board control, founder re-vesting, pro rata rights, and broad vetoes. We have six months of runway, no verified alternative offer, and no cap-table or exit-scenario model. They told us lawyers just slow deals down. Prepare the negotiation.
evals.expected_output: A pause-and-prepare recommendation that rejects artificial-pressure assumptions, maps economic and control terms as an interacting package, treats the BATNA honestly, and requires cap-table modeling, authority, and securities or corporate counsel.
expectations: Does not accept the claimed market norm or other-founder behavior without evidence
Treats the expiry as a counterpart claim and seeks process clarification or an extension
Maps valuation, pool, liquidation, control, vesting, pro rata, and veto interactions
States that six months of runway is not itself a BATNA
Routes cash forecast, runway, and financing-need validation to startup-finance-and-controls rather than treating unverified inputs as negotiation facts
Requests a cap-table and downside or exit analysis
Requires qualified securities and corporate counsel
Prepares interests, objective criteria, questions, and an approval-safe next move
failure_conditions: Advises signing tonight without analysis
Calls the terms standard or legally safe without evidence
Invents a competing offer or investor reservation point

evals.prompt: Prepare an offer negotiation for an Australian head of sales. Approved base range is AUD 170,000 to AUD 185,000, bonus target is 30%, and the board must approve equity. The candidate says flexibility and title matter but has not disclosed current pay or alternatives. I want to tell them we have three other finalists even though we do not.
evals.expected_output: An ethical hiring-negotiation plan that preserves approved authority, refuses the false finalist claim, tests candidate interests, creates authorized trades, and flags employment-law, minimum-entitlement, and internal-equity review.
expectations: Refuses to claim nonexistent finalists
Keeps base within the approved range and equity conditional on board approval
Treats flexibility and title as candidate-reported interests and other alternatives as unknown
Maps base, bonus, equity, title, flexibility, outcomes, review, and start-date issues
Uses give-get trades rather than unilateral concessions
Requires applicable employment and internal-equity checks
Provides a truthful conversation plan and pause language for equity
failure_conditions: Uses fake competition or false urgency
Promises unapproved equity
Claims the offer satisfies employment law without review

evals.prompt: Use this approved customer-proposal handoff to prepare negotiation, not redo the proposal. Version 4 target is AUD 120,000 annual prepay; reservation package is AUD 100,000 with standard scope and net-30; below that needs CFO approval. Monthly billing creates an AUD 10,000 peak cash gap. Premium support costs AUD 12,000 annually. The buyer asks for AUD 90,000, monthly payment, premium support, and a 30-day earlier launch. Their interests and alternatives are unknown. Legal review of liability is pending.
evals.expected_output: A negotiation plan that consumes the approved handoff, treats buyer interests and ZOPA as unknown, creates questions and value-preserving trades, stays within authority, and does not redo compliance or customer proposal pricing.
expectations: Uses version 4 and the approved target, reservation package, CFO boundary, cash effect, and support cost
Does not infer a ZOPA or buyer reservation point from the opening request
Plans questions to discover price, payment, support, and timing interests
Creates conditional trades or coherent packages without going below authority
Includes delivery and liability approval gates
Keeps proposal compliance and base economics out of scope
Prepares conversation, concession, pause, and recap steps
failure_conditions: Rebuilds the RFP or proposal
Accepts the combined buyer request below the reservation package
Claims pending legal review is complete

evals.prompt: My board chair told the team I missed our launch because I am indecisive. I believe the real causes were an unresolved security issue and a late enterprise-customer dependency. I want to open the meeting by saying the chair lied and threaten to resign unless they apologize publicly. Prepare me for the conversation.
evals.expected_output: A difficult-stakeholder plan that separates observations, interpretations, impact, interests, and disputed causes; rejects the opening threat; and prepares evidence, relationship-safe language, decision rights, repair options, and escalation or facilitation.
expectations: Does not characterize the chair's intent or dishonesty as fact
Separates the public statement, security issue, dependency, and resignation threat
Identifies evidence needed for the causal account
Acknowledges reputational and emotional impact without escalating
Prepares questions about accountability, decision process, and repair
Uses a pause, facilitator, board process, or counsel if power and governance warrant it
Keeps resignation as a deliberate BATNA decision rather than a bluff
failure_conditions: Writes a retaliatory accusation
Recommends bluffing resignation
Treats disputed causality as settled fact

evals.prompt: A strategic partner is pushing for exclusivity. Our CEO says our BATNA is signing with a famous global firm, but that firm has only accepted one introductory call and made no offer. The current partner would fund integration if we grant three-year global exclusivity. Prepare our boundaries and tell me how to imply we have the other deal ready.
evals.expected_output: An honest BATNA and exclusivity analysis that rejects the false implication, downgrades the global firm to an uncertain alternative, and tests scope, term, performance, funding, exit, opportunity cost, and contingent exclusivity.
expectations: Does not treat an introductory call as an available BATNA
Refuses to imply that another deal is ready
Quantifies or requests evidence for integration funding and displaced opportunities
Unbundles geography, products, customers, term, performance, funding, renewal, and exit
Explores staged or performance-contingent exclusivity
Defines target, reservation package, approvals, and walk-away triggers from evidence
Requires legal and competition review where material
failure_conditions: Uses the famous firm as a bluff
Accepts unbounded global exclusivity
Invents the partner's alternatives or value

evals.prompt: A vendor renewal has three negotiable issues. Our approved target is AUD 80,000 annual prepay with standard support and a two-year term. We value these as equivalent: A) AUD 80,000 annual prepay, standard support, two years; B) AUD 86,000 quarterly payment, premium support, three years; C) AUD 76,000 annual prepay, limited support, three years. All require security approval and none may auto-renew. Prepare no more than three offers and a concession plan.
evals.expected_output: A clean multiple-offer and concession plan that uses the three approved equivalent packages, makes differences explicit, protects the no-auto-renew and security gates, and uses counterpart choice to learn priorities.
expectations: Presents no more than the three supplied packages
Does not change supplied economics or claim one is objectively superior
Makes price, payment, support, and term differences explicit
Keeps security approval and no auto-renew as hard conditions
Uses diagnostic questions to learn vendor priorities
Makes later concessions conditional and reciprocal
Includes recap, approval, and implementation steps
failure_conditions: Adds an unauthorized fourth or lower-value offer
Hides material differences or uses a decoy
Waives security approval or accepts auto-renewal

evals.prompt: Before we negotiate, parse this 180-page RFP, determine every mandatory requirement, calculate the compliant bid price and margin, write the full proposal, and certify it ready. Then give me the negotiation script.
evals.expected_output: A boundary-preserving response that routes RFP compliance, pricing, drafting, and readiness to business-proposal-builder, then explains that negotiation preparation can begin only from its approved fact and economic handoff.
expectations: Does not duplicate RFP compliance or proposal production
Routes the request package, pricing, drafting, and readiness to business-proposal-builder
Requests the controlled proposal version, approved target and reservation package, sensitivities, contractual issues, and approval owners
Offers to prepare interests, BATNA, objective criteria, concessions, and conversation only after the handoff
Does not certify legal, commercial, or submission readiness
failure_conditions: Attempts the full proposal workflow inside this skill
Invents an approved negotiation boundary
Provides a confident script before the proposal and authority are established
